correctness.rationale: Unique hub has degree >=4, all other degrees 2; four variables define degree >=3. Finite-distance formulas on the hub-deleted graph have width <=4 despite unbounded depth. With N at least each component diameter, P_(ell,N) identifies precisely the petals of length ell, so k representatives test count thresholds <=k. For sufficiency, a permanent k-pebble matching of full-length petal paths works because before a fresh component assignment at most k-1 other petals are occupied. The closed count, minimum model and strictness follow. The included standalone finite color-refinement program verifies 95 decompositions, 13 selected equivalence pairs and 12 cardinality cases; computations are corroborative, not the proof.

value.rationale: A motivated exact structural classification for connected one-cut-vertex cactus graphs, not an arbitrary finite slice: it isolates precisely what k-variable logic retains about arbitrary mixed cycle-petal lengths. Definability of the single hub and finite path metric without a named parameter, sharp component-multiplicity truncations, a closed spectrum over every length alphabet, canonical minimum models, and an infinite strict hierarchy provide reusable information for broader cactus decompositions. The statement is limited to widths >=4; no unsupported general implication is asserted.
